get.summary: Downloads a blob. Authenticated by the bearer token or a presigned download URL.

put.summary:
Uploads bytes under their blake3 digest. Idempotent; rejected if the bytes do not match.
Authenticated by the bearer token or a presigned upload URL.

get.summary: Gets a change.

post.summary: Approves a change's latest revision as the caller, who must be a human.
Closes a change without merging.
Comments on a revision of a change, the latest by default, optionally on a line of a file.

get.summary:
What a revision of a change changes: the files that differ between the revision's base and
head in the repository's mirror, each with its unified patch as git prints it. A patch over
256 KiB is left out and its file marked truncated.

parameters.name: revision
parameters.description: The revision, from 1; the latest when omitted.

post.summary:
Merges a change: its latest revision's checks must have passed, it must be based on the
target branch's head, and changes to protected paths need a human approval. Igloo pushes
the revision to the target branch as one squashed commit naming the change.

Asks for another revision, carrying the comments made since the previous request. A change
made by a task sends them to its agent as its next turn.

Records the source branch's current head as the next revision; an unchanged head records
nothing.

get.summary: Lists the runs of a change, one per revision, oldest first.

Streams a notice per committed event as server-sent events: `id` is the event's sequence,
`event` its kind, `data` an `EventNotice`. `repo` keeps only events of that repository's
resources. `after`, or else `Last-Event-ID`, resumes after that sequence; without either the stream
starts at the log's current head and sends only events committed after it opened, and
`after=0` replays everything. Events are sent in sequence order, each once. Comments keep the connection alive every 15 seconds.

parameters.name: repo
parameters.description: Only events of this repository's resources

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Resume after this sequence; 0 replays the whole log; the current head when absent

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Resume after this sequence when `after` is absent

get.summary: Gets a job.

Streams a job's output as server-sent events: `stdout` and `stderr` events whose id resumes
the stream through `Last-Event-ID`, then one `end` event with the finished job.
Lists repositories, oldest first.

post.summary: Registers a repository.

get.summary: Gets a repository.

Lists a repository's changes, oldest first unless `order=newest`, optionally only those at
the given phases. Open changes carry their merge readiness.

parameters.name: phase
parameters.description: Only changes at this phase; repeatable

post.summary: Opens a change proposing a branch pushed to the forge; its head is the first revision.

put.summary: Sets the dotfiles new workspaces of the repository are set up with.

delete.summary: Clears the dotfiles of the repository.

get.summary: Lists a repository's runs, newest first, a page at a time.
Lists the names of a repository's secrets; values are never returned.

put.summary: Sets or replaces a secret. The body is its value, as text.

get.summary:
Lists the snapshots a repository recorded under keys, warm and agent, ordered by key, with
when each was last used. Sizes are not reported yet.

post.summary:
Snapshots a repository at a commit: the checkout under `/workspace`, with a shallow `.git`,
over an optional base snapshot. A branch is fetched from the forge first.

get.summary:
Lists a repository's tasks, oldest first unless `order=newest`, optionally only those at the
given phases.

parameters.name: phase
parameters.description: Only tasks at this phase; repeatable

post.summary: Creates a task: the agent starts from the head of the repository's default branch.

Opens a workspace on a branch of a repository for the caller. It starts at once: its sandbox
is forked from the repository's warm snapshot at the branch head.

get.summary: Gets a run.
Lists sandboxes, ordered by id, optionally filtered by labels (`label=key=value`, repeatable).

post.summary: Creates a sandbox from a registered snapshot.

get.summary: Gets a sandbox.

post.summary: Runs a process in a sandbox as a job.

Seals a running sandbox into a snapshot. The seal completes in the background; poll it with
`GET /v1/seals/{id}`.
Stops a sandbox. Idempotent.

get.summary:
Opens an interactive terminal in a running sandbox: upgrades to a WebSocket speaking the
subprotocol `igloo.terminal.v1`.
get.description:
With `mode=read_only` the caller watches: the server runs its own view of the sandbox (a
command of the caller's is refused) and drops every input frame, so nothing the caller sends
reaches the sandbox. The default `read_write` forwards input. In the sandbox of a task it is
refused (409) unless the caller is the person who took the task over, and it stops forwarding
input once the task is handed back.

Binary frames carry the terminal's bytes in both directions. Text frames carry JSON control
messages: the client sends `TerminalClientFrame` (resize); the server sends one
`TerminalServerFrame` (exit) and closes the socket when the process ends. Closing the socket
kills the process. Authenticated like the rest of the API; a browser, which cannot set headers
on a WebSocket, offers the subprotocol `igloo.bearer.<token>` as well.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The program and its arguments, one value each; the default shell when omitted

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: `read_only` to watch, which takes no command; `read_write` (the default) to type

101.description: Switching protocols to the WebSocket subprotocol `igloo.terminal.v1`

get.summary: Gets a seal.

put.summary:
Uploads the layer that completes a seal, as a tar archive. Authenticated only by the
presigned URL handed to the sandbox's worker.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: `full` for a whole root file system

post.summary: Registers a snapshot of uploaded layers, over a base snapshot's layers if one is named.
Pulls a public container image from its registry and registers its layers as a snapshot.

get.summary: Gets a snapshot.
Reports what the blob store holds and what its latest sweep reclaimed.
Gets a task.

post.summary:
Cancels a task and stops its sandbox. Cancelling an ended task changes nothing, except that
a task that failed collecting its commits stops the sandbox it kept for recovery.

Hands a task back, as the person who took it over, once its last turn ended and its commits
became a revision (until then the request is refused with `task.turn_running`). The sandbox
is read for what the person changed, without touching it, and the task's next turn is asked
about the commits they added and the changes they left uncommitted. Uncommitted work stays in
place. Handing back a task already being handed back changes nothing.

Takes a task over for the caller, who must be a person: the caller's terminal in the task's
sandbox (`GET /v1/sandboxes/{id}/terminal?mode=read_write`) becomes writable and no turn
starts until they hand the task back. A running turn is not interrupted. The sandbox keeps
running until the task ends. Taking over a task the caller already holds changes nothing.

get.summary:
A task's transcript from a position on: what its tool said and did, turn by turn, read from
its output with secrets masked. Poll with `after` set to the last response's `next`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The first position to return; 0 when absent.

get.summary: Lists the workers, ordered by id, with what their sandboxes hold of them.
Lists the caller's workspaces, oldest first.
Gets a workspace.

delete.summary: Deletes a workspace: its sandbox is stopped without sealing and its changes are dropped.

post.summary:
Starts a workspace: a sandbox resumes from what its last stop sealed. Starting a running
workspace changes nothing; a workspace that is stopping starts again once it has stopped.

Stops a workspace: its changes are sealed, then its sandbox stops. Stopping a stopped
workspace changes nothing.

revision.description: The revision; the latest when omitted.

line.description: The line of `path` it is about, from 1.

repo.description: The repository the sandbox works on (`repo_...`); its secrets become available to jobs.

base.description: A snapshot whose layers go underneath, such as an imported image.

base.description: The commit the diff starts from: the revision's base.

The dotfiles new workspaces of a repository are set up with: the repository is cloned and
the install command run in the clone, once, when a workspace is created.

install.description:
The shell command run in the clone; a failure is reported and does not fail the
workspace.

EventNotice.description:
What `GET /v1/events` sends as the `data` of each server-sent event: which resource changed
and when, never the domain payload. Clients refetch the resource.

kind.description: The event kind, such as `igloo.run.passed`; also the SSE `event`.

repo.description: The repository the resource belongs to, when it has one.

resource_type.description: The kind of resource the event belongs to, such as `run`.

sequence.description: The event's position in the global log; also the SSE `id`.

ExecRequest.description: Runs a process in a sandbox.

env.description: Extra environment, layered over the sandbox's.

secrets.description: Secrets of the sandbox's repository to expose as environment variables, by name.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the process may run, 1 to 86400 seconds; one hour when omitted.

FieldError.description: One invalid field of a request.

FileChangeStatus.description: How a file differs in a change's diff.

FileDiffResource.description:
One file of a change's diff.

A file has a `patch` unless it is binary or `truncated`.

additions.description: Lines added; 0 for a binary file.

deletions.description: Lines removed; 0 for a binary file.

patch.description:
The unified patch exactly as git prints it, from its `diff --git` header on. Absent for
a binary file and when `truncated`.

path.description: Its path after the change; for a deleted file, the path it had.

previous_path.description: The path a renamed file had before.

truncated.description: Whether the patch was left out for exceeding [`FileDiffResource::MAX_PATCH_BYTES`].

platform.description: `os/architecture`, such as `linux/arm64`; the server's architecture when omitted.

JobPhase.description: Where a job is in its lifecycle.

ended_at.description: When it finished, failed or was cancelled; absent until it has.

secrets.description: The repository secrets it is given, by name.

started_at.description: When its process started; absent until it has.

timeout_seconds.description: How long the process may run.

media_type.description: How the blob is encoded; `tar` when omitted.

MediaType.description: How a layer blob is encoded.

What stands between an open change and its merge, by the rules merging applies. Merging

approval.description: The approval of the latest revision.

checks.description: The checks of the latest revision.

humans.

token_secret.description: The secret holding the forge token.

base.description: Where it forked from the target branch.

TerminalMode.description:
Whether the caller of a terminal may type into the sandbox.

A read-only terminal runs a view chosen by the server (the sandbox's working tree status and
recent commits, refreshed every few seconds), never a program of the caller's, and the server
drops every byte the caller sends; it never writes to the sandbox. A read-write terminal runs
the requested program or the default shell and forwards input. The sandbox of a task is
writable only to the person who took the task over.

oneOf.description:

code.description: The process's exit code (128 + signal when killed by a signal).

oneOf.description: Why the terminal ended without an exit code.

TerminalServerFrame.description: A text frame the server sends.

turn.description: The turn it belongs to, from 1.

sandboxes.description: Sandboxes it holds, starting or ready.

sandbox.description: Its sandbox, while it has one. Its terminal is the sandbox's.

snapshot.description: The snapshot its last stop sealed, which holds everything the workspace has.
